messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] What is Fval and P val in QTL file generated in rqtl
parts:
Ah. What was confusing to me was that you showed just four columns, but the output of summary(fitqtl), in the "drop one QTL at a time" part, will have seven columns.

The "F value" column is the more traditional statistic for multiple linear regression: the mean regression sum of squares divided by the mean error sum of squares. The mean regression sum of squares is (type III SS) / df, with the values from the first two columns in that row (which you didn't show). The mean error sum of squares is from the "error" row in the "full model result", which is the table that preceded this "drop one qtl at a time" table.

The p-value (F) is derived from that F statistic and the two degrees of freedom. In contrast, Pvalue(Chi2) is derived by taking LOD/(2 log 10) and treating it as approximately chi-squared distributed under the null.

karl
